'''David Lodge''' (born April 1, 1957) is an American [[biologist]]. He is best known for his work on the interrelated problems of [[invasive species]], [[land use]], and [[climate change]], and their [[synergistic]] impacts on water resources.

== Biography ==
Lodge is a 1975 graduate of Sewanee Academy (now [[St. Andrew's-Sewanee School]]) and received his B.S., ''[[summa cum laude]]'', in 1979 from [[Sewanee: The University of the South]]. As a [[Rhodes Scholarship|Rhodes Scholar]], he completed his D.Phil. from [[Oxford University]] in 1982. From 1983 to 1985, he taught at the University of Wisconsin&ndash;Madison. From 1985 to 2016, he served on the faculty of the [[University of Notre Dame]] as a professor of biology, the director of the Notre Dame Center for Aquatic Conservation, and the director of the Notre Dame Environmental Change Initiative. From 2011 to 2016, Lodge was the  Ludmilla F., Stephen J., and Robert T. Galla Professor of Biological Sciences. Since May 2016, Lodge has been a member of the faculty of [[Cornell University]] where he holds the Francis J. DiSalvo Directorship of the David R. Atkinson Center for a Sustainable Future.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2015/08/biologist-david-lodge-named-director-atkinson-center |title=Biologist David Lodge named director of Atkinson Center  |work=[[Cornell Chronicle]] |date=2015-08-20 |accessdate=2016-07-01}}</ref>

Lodge is a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] and of the [[Ecological Society of America]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.esa.org/esa/tag/esa-fellows/ |title=Ecological Society of America announces 2016 fellows |publisher=Ecological Society of America |date=2016-06-01 |accessdate=2016-07-01}}</ref> He advocates for scientific approaches to manage invasive species in lake ecosystems.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1989/06/27/science/science-watch-bait-as-bully-a-crayfish-takes-over-fish-lakes.html |title=Science Watch; Bait as Bully: A Crayfish Takes Over Fish Lakes |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=1989-06-27 |accessdate=2016-07-01}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2003/06/19/opinion/biological-hazards-ahead.html |title=Biological Hazards Ahead  |work=The New York Times |date=2003-06-19 |accessdate=2016-07-01}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |url=http://content.time.com/time/health/article/0,8599,1962108,00.html |title=Asian Carp in the Great Lakes? This Means War! |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] |date=2010-02-09 |accessdate=2016-07-01}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://time.com/3000963/invasive-species-coming-soon-to-a-habitat-near-you/ |title=Invasive Species, Coming Soon to a Habitat Near You |magazine=Time |date=2014-07-17 |access-date=2016-07-01}}</ref> In 2014, Lodge served as a [[Jefferson Science Fellows Program|Jefferson Science fellow]] in the Office of Ocean and Polar Affairs at the [[United States Department of State]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://news.nd.edu/news/49268-biologist-david-lodge-named-jefferson-science-fellow/ |title=Biologist David Lodge named Jefferson Science Fellow |publisher=University of Notre Dame |date=2014-07-09 |accessdate=2016-07-01}}</ref>
